title: Quick Accent: Add a Latin character set
author: plovers

status.label: Design investigation queued
status.detail: The Classical Latin macron set is narrowly scoped and maps to Quick Accent's language registry, but no implementation-grade design is complete.

next_action.label: Develop Latin character-set design
next_action.reason: Define localization, ordering, mappings, and tests before exposing design approval.

judgment.rationale: The request supplies an exact six-letter mapping, a clear scenario, and a localized repository ownership path, so it is ready for design work without implying approval.
evidence: The requested mappings are A/E/I/O/U/Y to ā/ē/ī/ō/ū/ȳ for Classical Latin.
The current Quick Accent language enum has no Latin entry, and its canonical character registry has no ȳ mapping.
Quick Accent source documents the enum, registry, display order, localized resource, and mapping tests as the coordinated addition points.
judgment.recommended_action: Develop an implementation-grade design for a dedicated Latin set, including localization, ordering, uppercase behavior, and mapping tests; keep design_in_progress until reviewed.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent lacks a dedicated Classical Latin set and specifically cannot produce y with macron, while the desired six vowel mappings are fully specified.
known_information: The reporter supplied the complete proposed mapping and a concrete scholarly/educational use case.
Uppercase output can use Quick Accent's existing uppercase handling.
PowerAccent.Common.Language and CharacterMappings form the canonical registry.
Registry unit tests require every language enum value to appear exactly once.
inferences: The change appears localized and testable, but the stable identifier and localized display placement still need design confirmation.
A coherent Latin set is likely preferable to adding only ȳ to a miscellaneous set.
issue_context.analysis: The acceptance data and source owner are clear. The remaining work is implementation-grade design: choose the identifier and display placement, define the six mappings, and cover registry completeness and output behavior.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.Common/Language.cs and found no Latin enum value.
Inspected src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.Common/CharacterMappings.cs and found no ȳ mapping.
Repository history shows recent language additions using the same enum/registry/resource/test pattern.
